stimulus:
A compositor setting lead type works upside down and backwards, picking sorts
from the case into a composing stick held in the left hand. Capitals lived in the
upper case and small letters in the lower, which is where the names come from. To
justify a line, the compositor slips thin spaces of brass or copper between words
until the line is tight enough that the forme can be lifted without letters falling
out. A line that is too loose is called a 'pie' when it spills.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed re-challenge
ideas.description: Expose cells to a defined, transient AP-1-activating stimulus (e.g., TPA, TNF, or injury), let signaling return to baseline, then re-stimulate days to weeks later. Compare transcriptional output (RNA-seq) and chromatin accessibility against naive cells to test whether prior exposure leaves a lasting, AP-1-dependent change in response.

ideas.title: Time-resolved ATAC-seq/CUT&RUN of AP-1 occupancy and motif accessibility
ideas.description: Track chromatin accessibility, H3K27ac, and JUN/FOS binding at AP-1 motif-containing enhancers before, during, and long after the stimulus. Persistent opening or retained binding after AP-1 activity decays would indicate an epigenetic memory footprint, and ChromVAR-style motif analysis can quantify it.

ideas.title: Acute AP-1 depletion during memory maintenance phase
ideas.description: Use degron-tagged (dTAG/AID) or dominant-negative (A-FOS) AP-1 factors to remove AP-1 either only during the initial stimulus or only during the maintenance/recall phase. This separates AP-1 as the initiator of memory from AP-1 as the maintainer, and shows whether enhancer accessibility and primed responses persist without it.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome and lineage tracing of memory states
ideas.description: Perform single-cell RNA plus ATAC on stimulated and naive populations over time, combined with heritable barcodes or live reporters of AP-1 activity. This reveals whether memory is carried by cell-autonomous states inherited through divisions, and whether it correlates with prior AP-1 dynamics in individual cells.

ideas.title: Synthetic optogenetic AP-1 activation with sufficiency testing
ideas.description: Drive AP-1 factors (e.g., FOS/JUN) with light-inducible or pulsed expression at varied dose, duration, and frequency, then measure persistence of target gene expression and chromatin changes. Testing whether AP-1 alone is sufficient to create a lasting state, and how pulse patterns affect it, tests its causal role and tunability as a memory mechanism.
